options: Encrypting data so that its source cannot be identified
Grouping data based on an existing parameter without any tagging
Tagging something that is not identifiable when it comes from the source, based on a defined parameter
Deleting data that cannot be identified
Converting data from one format to another
questions.explanation: Data Labelling is about tagging something that is not identifiable coming from the source, based on some defined parameter.

questions.stem: On which kinds of data can Data Labelling be performed?
options: Both known data and unknown data
questions.explanation: Labelling can be done on known data and on unknown data as well.

questions.stem: On what basis does Data Classification group data?
options: Existing parameters only, with no human input
questions.explanation: Data Classification groups data based on manually labelled data and falls under Supervised Learning.

questions.stem: On what basis does Data Clustering group data?
questions.explanation: Data Clustering groups data based on an existing parameter and falls under Unsupervised Learning.

questions.stem: Why do specialised tools exist to tag or label unstructured datasets?
options: To compress the data for cheaper storage
To convert the data into relational tables
So the unstructured data can become input for Machine Learning models
questions.explanation: Specialised tools tag or label unstructured data so it can become input for Machine Learning models.

questions.stem: What can unstructured data labelled by an ML library then be used for?
options: As input to another ML model for Supervised Learning
questions.explanation: Certain libraries used in ML models label unstructured data, which can then become the input of another ML model for Supervised Learning.

questions.stem: Of Data Labelling, Data Classification and Data Clustering, which one falls under Unsupervised Learning?
questions.explanation: Data Clustering groups data on existing parameters and is Unsupervised Learning, whereas Data Classification uses labelled data and is Supervised Learning.

questions.stem: What development has driven the need for tools that label data?
options: The era of unstructured datasets, with data arriving in many formats
questions.explanation: Since the era of unstructured datasets, data comes in many formats, so specialised tools are needed to tag or label it.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Data Labelling and Data Classification?
options: Data Classification produces the labels that Data Labelling then applies
They are the same activity under different names
Data Labelling can only happen after clustering has finished
Data Classification never uses labelled data
Data Classification groups data using data that has been manually labelled
questions.explanation: Data Labelling tags data based on defined parameters, and Data Classification groups data based on that manually labelled data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of Data Labelling?
options: It tags data based on some defined parameter
It can be performed on unknown data
It can only be applied to data that is already identifiable at source
Specialised tools and ML libraries can perform it on unstructured data
Its output can feed a Supervised Learning model
questions.explanation: Data Labelling exists precisely to tag data that is not identifiable when it comes from the source.
